title: Does Duolingo teach you to speak?

paragraphs: A viral post by a user who lost a 2,061-day Duolingo streak exposed a fundamental flaw in the language-learning platform: years of daily app use failed to deliver actual conversational fluency.
Duolingo achieved massive financial success; it reached 1 billion dollars in revenue in 2025. How? By prioritizing gamification features like notifications, streak freezes, and leaderboards.

However, the company faced severe backlash after firing contractors to replace language courses with lower-quality generative AI content. This hyper-focus on user engagement over educational value eventually triggered a massive market correction. Duolingo’s stock plummeted roughly 80 percent from its peak near 544 dollars down to around 101 dollars by spring 2026. Investors grew skeptical as daily active user growth slowed, and law firms opened securities fraud investigations regarding potentially misleading growth metrics.

The dramatic financial collapse demonstrated that while Duolingo successfully optimized user habits, push notifications, and short-term corporate revenue, it failed to teach users how to speak new languages fluently.

paragraphs: A Duolingo user lost a 2,061-day streak and realized she still couldn’t speak Spanish fluently. This showed a big problem with the popular language app.

Duolingo became very rich by using games, daily streaks, and notifications to keep people using the app every day. The company also replaced many human workers with cheap AI to build its courses, which made the lessons worse. Even though the company earned a lot of money, investors started to worry that users were not actually learning anything. The company’s stock price dropped by 80 percent by early 2026. Lawyers also started investigating the company for confusing investors about user growth.
In the end, Duolingo created a great game to keep people clicking, but it failed at its main job: teaching people how to talk to real speakers.

paragraphs: A woman uses Duolingo for 2,061 days. She loses her daily streak. She can see that she still can not speak Spanish.

Duolingo uses games, points, and notifications to make people use the app every day. The company also fires real teachers and uses AI computers to make quick lessons. But the lesson quality is bad. In 2026, the company loses a lot of money. People see that the app is not teaching real language skills.
Duolingo builds a game, but it does not help people speak to others.
